enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
506 PM MST Tue Nov 17 2026

...New AVIATION...


.KEY MESSAGES... Updated at 1004 AM MST Tue Nov 17 2026

 - Isolated rain showers across Western New Mexico this evening,but 
   otherwise dry.

 - Slightly above normal temperatures over the next few days 
   before becoming slightly cooler this weekend. 

 - Breezy winds expected Friday into early Saturday morning.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1004 AM MST Tue Nov 17 2026

This afternoon and tonight... This afternoon will be dry and 
breezy, because of a storm system moving through the Rockies. 
Highs across the area will climb to the mid to upper 60s, 
approaching that 70 degree mark. This evening and into the 
overnight an upper level low will cause southwesterly winds and 
bring a surge of some moisture into the mid levels. This will 
bring a slight chance for isolated showers in the Gila and Black 
range regions this evening into late tonight. Areas of higher 
elevations with West to East facing passes could see a high gust 
or two up to 40 mph as the low passes north of the region.

Wednesday through Friday...
Tomorrow upper level ridging will bring high pressure back to the
region bringing fair weather with light winds until Friday. Highs
will climb into the low to mid 70s through Friday. Another upper 
level trough will begin to move into the area on Friday. 
Southwesterly winds will return and bring breezy winds to the area
with gusts to 30 mph. Although the threat of rain will remain 
mainly north of our region, a non-zero chance of an isolated light
shower will be possible in the Gila/Back Range region, given some
cyclonic vorticity and modest moister in the mid levels. 

Saturday into Early Next Week... Moving into the weekend another 
ridge will create calm and fair weather for most of the weekend, 
temperatures will be slightly cooler, following the storm system 
from friday. Early next week another trough will move into the 
area bringing our next chance of precipitation, but it is still 
too early to determine how much rain there will be or how 
widespread it will be. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 459 PM MST Tue Nov 17 2026

An approaching upper level storm system will give us some clouds
and even a few rain showers, mainly in the Gila Region. Best
chances for ceilings (BKN050) will be at KTCS. Most of the showers
will be north of the area by around by midnight, but some clouds
will linger into the morning. By late morning and into Tuesday
afternoon we will have unlimited ceilings. Wind are becoming light
and it looks like those light and variable winds will dominate
tonight through most of the day on Tuesday.
 
&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1004 AM MST Tue Nov 17 2026

Not much in the way of fire concerns as RHs remain unseasonably
high. The Gila zone could see a light shower overnight tonight,
otherwise mainly dry through this weekend. Breezy afternoon winds
Friday and Saturday, just enough to improve vent rates.
Temperatures will remain slightly above normal through Friday,
cooling to slightly below normal Saturday and Sunday as a Pacific
cold front moves through. 

Min RH: Lowlands 35-45% Wed/Thu, decreasing to 20-30% Fri/Sat.
Mountains 35-45% Wed/Thu, decreasing to 25-35% Fri/Sat. Vent rates
poor-fair Wed/Thu becoming good-very good Fri/Sat.
